t: For necessary expenses for construction at the federally owned civil airports in the vicinity of the District of Columbia, $16,200,000, to remain available until September 30, 1983.

fable.w: This is a plain appropriation of funds for construction at federally owned airports. There is no tempting contrary reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For necessary expenses for construction at the federally owned civil airports in the vicinity of the District of Columbia, $16,200,000, to remain available until September 30, 1983.

opus.w: This provision only sets aside money for construction at federally owned airports and says how long the funds remain available. It does not involve any outside party, such as states, local governments or the public, in a federal decision. Although the airports affect the surrounding area, the text creates no consultation, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: For necessary expenses for construction at the federally owned civil airports in the vicinity of the District of Columbia, $16,200,000, to remain available until September 30, 1983.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation clause authorizing funds for construction. It does not require or recommend any form of participation, such as public hearings, advisory committees, or consultation with outside entities. The text only specifies the amount and purpose of the funding.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses for construction at the federally owned civil airports in the vicinity of the District of Columbia, $16,200,000, to remain available until September 30, 1983.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "construction at... airports" implies public use or interaction, but the text itself is purely an appropriation clause. It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory process involving non-federal entities. It simply authorizes spending.
